breakdown.description: The prompt sets the free-end rotation to zero, even though a cantilever’s free end is generally free to rotate under an end point load.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification applies the zero-rotation boundary condition at x = 0 (the fixed end), not at the free end. It also specifies calculating the slope at the free end (x = L), implying the free end is allowed to rotate. This correctly avoids the error of setting the free-end rotation to zero.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats the bending moment as constant and equal to P L over the entire span, even though the cantilever moment varies linearly from the free end to the fixed end.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly repeats the incorrect assumption: 'Use the given assumption of constant moment M = P × L = 2500 × 800 = 2000000 N-mm over the full span' and sets up the differential equation with this constant moment. The ground truth removes this erroneous instruction entirely, expecting the correct linearly varying moment M(x) = P(L - x) to be used. The agent failed to fix this inconsistency.
